title: Naming the measurement pathologies, placing the headline
summary:
Primary-full-text dossier for iteration 5. Deliverables: research_report.md (S0-S10) and research_out.json carrying the three ready-to-paste Discussion passages, a 7-row neighbour table, two branch-specific residual-novelty paragraphs, a 25-row query log, and a 16-entry BibTeX block. Every number is a verbatim quote with an anchor or is marked NOT FOUND / NOT OBTAINED / INHERITED.

THREE FRONT-MATTER RESOLUTIONS. (1) The 2506.24056 coverage conflict is NOT a version drift: 97.5-99.8% (fraction of toxic prompts where the ALIGNED gap exceeds the BASE gap) and 92.1% [89.4-94.2] (Qwen2.5-0.5B's position-1 decision census; Llama 98.8%, gemma 96.0%) are BOTH in v2 and measure different things. Cite 92-99% for position-1 validity, 97.5-99.8% for 'alignment widens the gap'. (2) The 0.464 blocker is RESOLVED from the shipped table, no placeholder needed: ourAMS rho = 0.358 (19 members) vs 0.821 (7 lineages), gap = 0.4636; the -0.929/-0.376 pair (diff 0.553) is a DIFFERENT quantity (oriented Delta, v2 carrier); median 0.238 / max 0.557 / 5-of-16 sign flips is a third. The drafter must name which pair of cells. (3) HURTADO VERDICT: H-G's novelty survives, but the plan's assumed distinction is WRONG - Hurtado's labels come from a behavioural oracle (Qwen3Guard), not a provenance tag, and his rho is explicitly 'one scalar per model'. The four surviving residuals are: attested reference required and spoofable; BINARY label vs graded refusal rate; 4 families vs 11; full weight download required. H-G may NOT claim 'first model-level cheap safety score validated against behaviour'.

LOGIT-GAP FULLY EXTRACTED (v2, full text). NO cross-model margin-vs-behaviour correlation exists - all 28 correlation matches inspected; every one is token-level, suffix-level, or cited from Bai et al. The abstract's co-variation is 'across suffix strategies' and is self-labelled an internal consistency check. Token lists recovered verbatim. CRITICAL CAVEAT NOT PREVIOUSLY RECORDED: their affirmative token is chosen PER PROMPT as the highest-logit one, making their gap an attack-relevant MINIMUM; a fixed-list max is a different estimand and must be declared.

CANONICAL SOURCES PINNED AND QUOTED. Leakage = Kapoor & Narayanan L3.3 Sampling bias in test distribution (exact label; L1.2 for the statistics half). Aggregation = Robinson 1950, with the sign flip read out of the paper: nativity x illiteracy is +.118 individual, -.526 (48 states), -.619 (9 divisions) - do NOT use the trio recalled in the plan. Openshaw CATMOG 38 supplies the scale/aggregation definitions and the devastating 'for a 6 region aggregation of the 99 Iowa counties the range of possible correlations is between -.99 and +.99'. Simpson 1951 verified (and Semantic Scholar's 'A. Simpson' is WRONG; the byline is E. H. Simpson). Small-sample = Schoenbrodt & Perugini 2013 with full Table 1: POS_crit at w=.10/80% is 252/238/212/181 for rho=.1/.2/.3/.4, so n=28 is 6.5-9x below stability - state this DELIBERATELY. NEW FIND: a 2018 CORRIGENDUM exists (DOI 10.1016/j.jrp.2018.02.010) and must be cited alongside.

CORRECTIONS TO OUR RECORDS. Mehta's LOQO figures are 0.43/0.87 in primary text, NOT 0.425/0.870 - quote two decimals. His 0.761 IS verified verbatim, as is the sharper control (AUROC 0.63 on a condition where the effect cannot exist). arXiv:2607.28685's -0.64@n=7 -> +0.02@n=18 is CONFIRMED plus a previously unrecorded and stronger clause: 'a quarter of random size-7 subsets show |rho| >= 0.5'. AMS verified at 14 configs / 4 families / Pearson -0.546 (p=0.043) - but its SPEARMAN is -0.423 at p=0.13, which is the directly comparable statistic and is not significant. NEW NEIGHBOUR: arXiv:2602.09434 (Xu & Sheng), refusal vectors over 76 offspring models at 100% base-family identification - outcome is MODEL IDENTITY, the clean provenance-vs-behaviour distinction the plan expected from Hurtado. arXiv:2603.27412's real title is 'The Geometry of Harmful Intent', not 'LatentBiopsy'.

SATURATION: the 13 scholarly-mode zeros are NOT credible (OpenAlex returned oncology and climate models); the claim is carried by arXiv-scoped search plus five harvested related-work sections. C1: no work validates such a score against judged behaviour at >=20 lineages or >=10 families; family-axis maximum anywhere is 4. C2: one direct hit only. TALLY for the COLLAPSES branch: 5 of 5 located model-level scores validate at <=4 families, 4 of 5 at <=14 checkpoints, and 0 of 5 use lineage-clustered resampling - lead with that last count.

NOT RESOLVED: iter-4 references numbered 11 and 23 (the numbered bibliography is in no readable workspace); Moreno-Torres full text (six routes failed, so NO quotation from it exists and it should be demoted to a citation without a quote).
answer:
See research_out.json (machine-readable) and research_report.md (S0-S10) for the full dossier with verbatim quotes and anchors. Headline findings, with citation numbers keyed to the sources list:

FRONT MATTER. (1) The arXiv:2506.24056 coverage conflict is resolved and is NOT a version drift: 97.5-99.8% and 92.1% [89.4-94.2] are both in v2 and are percentages of different things. The first is the fraction of 520 AdvBench toxic prompts on which the aligned model's gap exceeds the base model's; the second is the position-1 decision census for Qwen2.5-0.5B alone (Llama-3.2-1B 98.8%, gemma-2-2b 96.0%), with the residual 'concentrated on multi-token preambles' [1]. Cite 92-99% for position-1 validity and 97.5-99.8% for 'alignment widens the gap'; the paper's own summary is 'The position-1 assumption holds at 92-99% per-model coverage' [1]. Read and cite v2 (1 May 2026); v1 carried a different title.

(2) The 0.464 blocker is resolved from our own shipped table and needs no placeholder. ourAMS correlates with judged outcome at rho = 0.358 over 19 members and 0.821 over 7 lineages, a gap of 0.4636; the -0.929 vs -0.376 pair (difference 0.553) is the oriented Delta for the v2 carrier, a different quantity; and median 0.238 / max 0.557 / 5-of-16 sign flips is a third. All four exist under distinct keys with distinct definitions. The drafter must name which pair of cells in the sentence itself.

(3) Hurtado (arXiv:2607.01854) is the closest neighbour and the plan's assumed distinction is wrong. His labels come from a behavioural oracle - 'A behavioral oracle (Qwen3Guard, think-traces stripped) labels whether a checkpoint is uncensored' - and his score is explicitly 'one scalar per model' [7]. So it is genuinely model-level and behaviour-validated. Four residuals survive and are what H-G may claim: an attested reference model is required and is spoofable ('using the candidate as its own reference evades by construction'); the outcome is a binary uncensored label, not a graded refusal rate; the panel is 4 architecture families against our 11; and scoring 'means downloading its full weights' [7]. H-G may not claim to be the first model-level cheap safety score validated against behaviour.

LOGIT-GAP STEERING, FULL EXTRACTION. The scalar is theirs: 'the difference between the top refusal-token logit and the top affirmative-token logit at the first decoding step', quantifying 'the per-prompt safety margin that alignment provides' [1]. No cross-model correlation of that margin against behaviour exists anywhere in the paper - I grepped the full v2 text for correlation terms and inspected all 28 matches; every one is a within-pool token ranking (Spearman rho >= 0.818, unit = candidate token, and the authors disclaim its validity role), a pairwise failure correlation between suffixes, or a reward-proxy correlation cited from Bai et al. The abstract's co-variation is 'across suffix strategies' and is self-labelled 'an internal consistency check, since our method optimises gap closure' [1]. The only clustered analysis is family-clustered at n = 3 on attack deltas. There is no lineage treatment, and benign prompts appear once, only as a contrast for a distribution figure. Token lists are recovered verbatim from Appendix B.1. One caveat we had not recorded and that must govern the reimplementation: the affirmative token is chosen per prompt as 'the one with the highest positive logit under the aligned model', making their gap an attack-relevant minimum rather than a fixed-list max [1].

PHENOMENON 1, LEAKAGE. Kapoor and Narayanan's taxonomy names our case exactly as 'L3.3 Sampling bias in test distribution' - 'choosing a non-representative subset of the dataset for evaluation ... the test set is no longer representative of the general population about which claims are made' - with 'L1.2 Pre-processing on training and test set' covering the statistics half [2]. The field-local instance is re-verified: Mehta's probe 'reached AUROC=0.761' under full-pool residualization, and he writes 'We initially treated this as our headline result. It was not' [12]. Correction to our records: the post-control figures in primary text are 0.43 and 0.87, not 0.425 and 0.870. The sharpest sentence is one we did not have: the same MLP 'reaches AUROC=0.63 on Llama' on a control where the effect cannot exist [12].

PHENOMENON 2, AGGREGATION. Robinson 1950 is the primary, and the numbers must be read out of the paper rather than recalled: colour x illiteracy is .203 individual, .773 at 48 states, .946 at 9 divisions; nativity x illiteracy is .118 individual but 'the ecological correlation ... is -.619! When the ecological correlation is computed on a state rather than a divisional basis, its value is -.526' [3]. His conclusion is one word: ecological correlations cannot validly substitute for individual ones [3]. Openshaw's CATMOG 38 supplies the two-component definition - the scale problem and, when the number of units is held constant, 'the aggregation problem' - and the strongest available quote for our sign flips: 'for a 6 region aggregation of the 99 Iowa counties the range of possible correlations is between -.99 and +.99' [4]. Openshaw & Taylor's own conclusion, quoted there, is the honest note for us: 'We have been able to find a wide range of correlations. We simply do not know why we have found them' [4]. Simpson 1951 is verified and should be cited in half a clause as the origin of the name, with the scope note that his setting is categorical contingency tables [6]; note that the Semantic Scholar record's author 'A. Simpson' is wrong, the byline reads E. H. Simpson [6, 17].

PHENOMENON 3, SMALL SAMPLES. Schoenbrodt and Perugini define the corridor of stability and the point of stability - 'that sample size from which value on the trajectory of the correlation does not leave the COS any more' - and conclude that 'in typical scenarios the sample size should approach 250 for stable estimates' [5]. Their Table 1 is specific to our band: at w = .10 and only 80% confidence, POS_crit is 252, 238, 212 and 181 for rho = .1, .2, .3, .4 [5]. Our n = 28 is therefore 6.5-9x below stability, and the paper should say so deliberately rather than have it said against it. A published 2018 corrigendum exists and must be cited alongside; its content could not be obtained [15]. The field-local precedent is confirmed verbatim and comes with a stronger clause than we had: the correlation 'moves from -0.64 at n=7 to +0.02 at n=18, and a quarter of random size-7 subsets show |rho| >= 0.5 despite the near-zero full-panel value' [13].

NEIGHBOUR RECONCILIATION. AMS is verified at 14 configurations over 4 families with leave-one-out accuracy 71% and Pearson r = -0.546 (p = 0.043) - but its rank-order statistic, the one directly comparable to a Spearman headline, is rho = -0.423 at p = 0.13 [8]. RAS requires 'a safety-aligned reference model' and a same-family target, and reports no coefficient, n, or resampling unit that I could locate [9]. AQI measures within-model cluster separation via DBS/Dunn/XBI/CHI and claims correlation with external judges without a locatable n or coefficient [10, 11]. Two neighbours not on the plan's list were found: Xu & Sheng use refusal vectors across 76 offspring models at 100% base-family identification, but the outcome is model identity, which is the clean provenance-versus-behaviour distinction the plan expected from Hurtado [14]; and Sokhansanj's 8,608-repository survey is the largest behavioural panel in the lane but carries no internal score [18].

SATURATION. The thirteen scholarly-mode queries returned zero qualifying hits, but that is not credible evidence - OpenAlex returned clinical guidelines, oncology and climate models for all thirteen, so it is not indexing 2026 preprints in this lane. The claim is carried by arXiv-scoped search and by the related-work sections of the five papers read in full. C1: no work validates a benchmark-free internal safety score against judged behaviour at 20 or more weight lineages or 10 or more architecture families; the family-axis maximum anywhere is 4. C2: one direct hit only [13]. The residual under both H-G branches is the conjunction - graded judged behaviour, reference-free, weights-free, 11 families, lineage-clustered inference - of which no located work has more than two. For the collapses branch, the tally built from primary text is the evidence: 5 of 5 located model-level scores validate at 4 or fewer families, 4 of 5 at 14 or fewer checkpoints, and 0 of 5 use lineage-clustered resampling. Lead with that last count.

CONFIDENCE AND WHAT WOULD CHANGE IT. High for the front matter, the logit-gap extraction and the five canonical sources read in full text. Low for Moreno-Torres, whose full text could not be obtained through six routes, so no quotation from it appears anywhere and it should be demoted to a citation without a quote [16]. Medium for saturation, whose honest form is 'not found by arXiv-scoped search or in five related-work sections', not 'does not exist'. Obtaining the RAS and AQI cross-model statistics would either strengthen the collapses tally or narrow the holds paragraph; reading arXiv:2602.22289 and arXiv:2603.18353 could produce a genuine C2 hit. Iteration-4 references numbered 11 and 23 could not be resolved because the numbered bibliography is not in any readable workspace, and no entries were invented.

follow_up_questions: RAS and AQI both claim their score correlates with behaviour but neither reports a coefficient, an n, or a resampling unit anywhere I could locate - is that genuinely absent from both, and if so does the collapses-branch tally become '2 of 5 published model-level safety scores report no quantitative criterion-validity statistic at all'?

Hurtado validates a per-model activation gap against binary behavioural-oracle labels on 273 checkpoints, so the honest comparison is binary-versus-graded outcome rather than provenance-versus-behaviour: should H-G additionally report its margin's AUROC against a binarised refusal-rate label, so the two are comparable on his metric and not only on ours?

Logit-Gap Steering picks the affirmative token per prompt as the highest-logit one, making their gap an attack-relevant minimum rather than a fixed-list max - does reimplementing their exact estimand versus a fixed-list max change our model-level rho, and should that be a preregistered sensitivity arm rather than an implementation footnote?

discussion_passages.cross_cutting_intro: Three of this paper's surviving results are measured instances of long-named methodological phenomena rather than new phenomena. We name each, cite its canonical statement, and claim only the instance. What we believe is our own is narrower and, we think, more useful: all three are demonstrated on THIS PAPER'S OWN previously published numbers, under the original code and the original preregistration, with the effect localised to the original block -- the archived 19-member analysis reproduces to the byte while the 33 newly added members do not. A methodological hazard that has been named for seventy-five years is not a contribution; a quantified, self-inflicted, localised instance of it inside a live interpretability result is a measurement, and it is the kind of measurement this literature does not currently produce.
discussion_passages.phenomenon_1_leakage: The item pool is a leakage surface, and this is a textbook leakage type. Kapoor and Narayanan's taxonomy of leakage in ML-based science names our case directly as [L3.3] Sampling bias in test distribution: "choosing a non-representative subset of the dataset for evaluation ... the test set is no longer representative of the general population about which claims are made" (Kapoor & Narayanan 2023), and the neighbouring [L1.2] covers the statistics-estimated-on-everything half of the same error. We claim no discovery here. We claim the measured instance: on the six depth-panel checkpoints, the SAME refusal axis moves from AUROC {{ARCHIVED_LO}}-{{ARCHIVED_HI}} when scored on the archived, steered item pool to 0.906-0.980 when scored on each model's own spontaneous text, with induction unchanged -- a read-versus-act conclusion decided entirely by which items the score was evaluated on. The field-local precedent is exact: Mehta reports that a probe scoring AUROC 0.761 under full-pool residualization falls to 0.43 on one model under leave-one-query-out with per-fold residualization, and scores 0.63 on a control condition where the effect being detected cannot exist (arXiv:2607.13346).
discussion_passages.phenomenon_1_limitations_variant: Our read-versus-act comparison is an instance of what Kapoor and Narayanan classify as [L3.3] sampling bias in the test distribution -- the pool on which the axis was scored was not the pool the claim was about -- and we report the instance, not the phenomenon.
discussion_passages.phenomenon_2_aggregation: The aggregation unit is a free parameter, and choosing it is choosing the answer. Robinson showed in 1950 that the same relationship computed at different levels of aggregation need not even agree in sign: the individual correlation between foreign birth and illiteracy is +.118, while "the ecological correlation between foreign birth and illiteracy ... is -.619! When the ecological correlation is computed on a state rather than a divisional basis, its value is -.526" (Robinson 1950), and he concluded that ecological correlations "cannot" validly substitute for individual ones. Openshaw's modifiable-areal-unit-problem literature separates this into a scale problem and an aggregation problem -- "any variation in results due to the use of alternative units of analysis when the number of units is held constant is termed the aggregation problem" -- and reports that for a six-zone aggregation of 99 Iowa counties "the range of possible correlations is between -.99 and +.99" (Openshaw 1984; Openshaw & Taylor 1979). Simpson's 1951 note is the origin of the paradox's name, though its setting is categorical contingency tables rather than a continuous rank correlation, so Robinson is the closer analogue. We do not claim aggregation bias as a finding; we claim a measured instance in which it moves this study's own headline by 0.464 and flips 5 of 16 signs. Concretely: holding the data, the score and the outcome fixed and changing only the counting unit, our headline score correlates with judged behaviour at rho = 0.358 over 19 members and at rho = 0.821 over 7 lineages -- a gap of 0.464 -- and across the 16 score x config cells the unit alone moves rho by a median of 0.238, by as much as 0.557, and reverses its sign in 5 of them.
discussion_passages.phenomenon_3_small_sample: Our seven-lineage panel was below the point of stability, and we can now say by how much. Schoenbrodt and Perugini define the corridor of stability and the point of stability -- "that sample size from which value on the trajectory of the correlation does not leave the COS any more" -- and conclude that "in typical scenarios the sample size should approach 250 for stable estimates" (Schoenbrodt & Perugini 2013; see also their 2018 corrigendum). Their Table 1 is specific about our regime: for true correlations of .1-.4, even at the most permissive setting they report (half-width w = +/-.10 at only 80% confidence), the critical point of stability is n = 252, 238, 212 and 181 respectively. We do not claim that small-sample correlations are unstable; that is theirs. We claim the measured instance, and we claim it against ourselves: quadrupling the panel from 7 to 28 weight lineages moves our own previously published Delta_A from +0.296 to +0.099 with a lineage-clustered interval of [-0.027, 0.244] that includes zero, and the effect is LOCALISED -- the archived 19-member block reproduces at +0.2963 byte-for-byte under the original code, while the 33 newly added members give -0.016. The published field-local precedent is arXiv:2607.28685, whose R-Judge/AgentHarm correlation "moves from -0.64 at n=7 to +0.02 at n=18, and a quarter of random size-7 subsets show |rho| >= 0.5 despite the near-zero full-panel value." We note against ourselves that n = 28 is still 6.5-9x below the point of stability for this effect-size band: the finding is the direction of travel under a fourfold panel increase, not a claim that +0.099 is the settled value.

logit_gap_extraction.unit_verbatim: This single scalar quantifies the per-prompt safety margin that alignment provides.
logit_gap_extraction.token_list_provenance_verbatim: we manually curated three token lists by prompting models with harmful, benign, and neutral queries and collecting first response tokens
logit_gap_extraction.critical_estimand_caveat: The affirmative term is chosen PER PROMPT as 'the one with the highest positive logit under the aligned model, so that the measured refusal-affirm gap ... is precisely the minimum decrement required for a successful jailbreak' [S E.1]. Their gap is an attack-relevant MINIMUM. If our reimplementation takes a plain max over a fixed list, that is a DIFFERENT ESTIMAND and must be stated.
logit_gap_extraction.refusal_token_noise_caveat: The refusal list includes 'However' and ' not', which will fire outside refusals. Inherit knowingly or replace with a stated alternative.
logit_gap_extraction.prompt_set: 520 AdvBench, toxic only. HarmBench n=200 for ASR. Benign prompts appear ONCE, only as a contrast for a distribution figure (Fig. 9) - no benign margin, no over-refusal analysis, no model-level benign analysis anywhere.
logit_gap_extraction.model_panel: 3 families (Qwen, Llama, Gemma), 0.5B-72B, 13 models in the ASR table.
logit_gap_extraction.cross_model_correlation_against_behaviou: NONE. Confirmed by grepping 'correlat|Spearman|per-model|across models|Kendall|rank correlation' over the full v2 PDF (28 matches, all inspected). Every correlation is (a) within-pool TOKEN ranking (Spearman rho >= 0.818, unit = candidate token, and the authors explicitly disclaim its validity role), (b) pairwise failure correlation between SUFFIXES, or (c) a reward-proxy correlation cited from Bai et al. The abstract's co-variation is 'across suffix strategies' and is self-labelled 'an internal consistency check, since our method optimises gap closure'.
logit_gap_extraction.closest_clustered_analysis: 'Family-clustered (n=3) deltas are consistent: Ours > GCG+SH on 3/3 families with mean +10.4 pp AdvBench (App. O).' - clusters ASR DIFFERENCES, not the margin, at n=3.
logit_gap_extraction.lineage_treatment: ABSENT. No clustering by weight lineage, no repeated-measures model, no treatment of Qwen2.5-0.5B and Qwen2.5-72B as non-independent.
logit_gap_extraction.concession_sentence: The scalar is not ours. Li and Liu define the refusal-affirmation logit gap at the first decoding step and establish that it is a meaningful per-prompt safety margin; what is ours is the model-level criterion validation of that scalar against judged behaviour, and the 28-lineage, 11-family panel with lineage-clustered inference that makes such a validation non-trivial.
logit_gap_extraction.honesty_sentence: This score is not harmful-prompt-free: like the per-prompt gap it generalises, it reads the margin on harmful prompts. What it saves is everything downstream - no generation, no judge, no benchmark, and no reference model.

residual_novelty_paragraphs.branch_holds: The cheapest score in its class -- {{N_FORWARD_PASSES, target 80}} forward passes per checkpoint, no generation, no judge, no benchmark, no reference model and no access to weight diffs -- predicts judged plain-harmful refusal rate at rho = {{RHO}} ({{CI_LO}}, {{CI_HI}}, lineage-clustered bootstrap; p = {{P_PERM}} against a Monte-Carlo lineage-permutation null) across {{N_LINEAGES, target 28}} weight lineages and {{N_FAMILIES, target 11}} architecture families. The score is read on harmful prompts, so it is not harmful-prompt-free; what it removes is everything downstream of the forward pass. We claim none of the following. We do not claim the scalar: the refusal-affirmation logit gap at the first decoding step is defined by Li and Liu (arXiv:2506.24056), who establish it as a per-prompt safety margin and validate it against their own attack's success rate across suffix strategies, not across models. We do not claim to be first on abliterated checkpoints: arXiv:2603.27412 already runs base/instruct/abliterated Qwen triplets. We do not claim the largest checkpoint panel: Hurtado (arXiv:2607.01854) audits 273 checkpoints. What is ours is the conjunction that none of them has: a model-level criterion validation of a first-decoding-step margin against a GRADED judged refusal rate, with no attested reference model and no weight access -- Hurtado's audit needs both, and RAS needs a family-scoped reference anchor -- over 11 architecture families rather than 3 or 4, with inference clustered on the weight lineage rather than the checkpoint, which is the unit the dependence actually lives at and which no paper in this lane currently uses. The comparison that makes the panel non-trivial is that AMS, the closest published attempt at exactly this validation, reports Pearson r = -0.546 (p = 0.043) over 14 configurations from 4 families -- and its rank-order statistic, the one directly comparable to ours, is rho = -0.423 at p = 0.13.
residual_novelty_paragraphs.branch_collapses: Every cheap activation- or logit-derived safety score we were able to test collapses when the validation panel is quadrupled from 7 to {{N_LINEAGES, target 28}} weight lineages: {{SCORE_TALLY}}. The claim we make is not that small-sample correlations are unstable -- Schoenbrodt and Perugini own that, and their Table 1 puts the point of stability for correlations in the .1-.4 band at n = 181-252 even at the most permissive corridor they report. The claim is specific to this lane and is a claim about its published evidence base: the validation panels on which benchmark-free internal safety scores currently rest are systematically an order of magnitude below the point of stability, and this is a direct measurement of what happens when one of them is quadrupled -- on the authors' own prior result, under the original code, with the effect localised to the original block. The tally supporting the first half is short enough to print. Of the model-level internal safety scores we could locate in primary text, AMS validates at 14 configurations over 4 families (Pearson r = -0.546, p = 0.043; Spearman rho = -0.423, p = 0.13); RAS validates against attack success rate across 3 families with no correlation coefficient, n, or resampling unit reported; AQI claims correlation with external judges without a locatable n or coefficient; Logit-Gap Steering validates a per-prompt margin against its own attack's ASR across suffix strategies, with family-clustered inference at n = 3; and only Hurtado exceeds 20 checkpoints -- at 273 -- but against a binary label, with an attested reference model and full weight access required, and with no lineage-clustered resampling in any of the five. Not one of them resamples on the weight lineage. Our own iteration-2 result at 7 lineages (Delta_A = +0.296) is a member of exactly that reference class, and it does not survive: at 28 lineages Delta_A = +0.099 with a lineage-clustered interval of [-0.027, 0.244], and the 33 newly added members give -0.016 while the archived 19 reproduce +0.2963 to the byte. The published field-local precedent for the mechanism is arXiv:2607.28685, where a benchmark correlation "moves from -0.64 at n=7 to +0.02 at n=18, and a quarter of random size-7 subsets show |rho| >= 0.5 despite the near-zero full-panel value." We note against ourselves that 28 is still 6.5-9x below the point of stability; the result is the direction of travel under a fourfold increase, not a settled value.

saturation.channel_caveat: The scholarly channel (Q1-13, OpenAlex) is NOT a credible zero: it returned topically unrelated results (clinical guidelines, oncology, climate models, root ecology) for all thirteen, i.e. it is not indexing 2026 arXiv preprints in this lane. The saturation claim is carried by the arXiv-scoped searches (Q15-18) plus the related-work sections of the five papers read in full text.
saturation.C1_verdict: NO work found validating a benchmark-free activation- or logit-derived safety score against judged behaviour across >=20 weight lineages or >=10 architecture families. Located maxima: 273 checkpoints / 4 families against a BINARY label with an attested reference (Hurtado); 76 offspring models against MODEL IDENTITY (Xu & Sheng). Maximum on the family axis is 4.
saturation.C2_verdict: ONE direct hit (arXiv:2607.28685, agent-safety BENCHMARKS not internal scores). No published negative panel-scaling result for cheap internal safety scores was found - this is what makes the COLLAPSES branch non-vacuous. Two unread near-misses surfaced and are NOT claimed: arXiv:2602.22289, arXiv:2603.18353.
saturation.residual_under_both_branches: NOT 'first model-level cheap safety score' (Hurtado, RAS, AMS are all model-level) and NOT 'first on abliterated checkpoints' (arXiv:2603.27412). It is the CONJUNCTION: graded judged behaviour + reference-free + weights-free + >=10 families + lineage-clustered inference. No located work has more than two of the five.
saturation.self_replication_precedent: Largely NOT FOUND. Closest available register: arXiv:2607.28685's 'a small-panel failure mode we walked into', and arXiv:2607.13346 S4.3's 'We initially treated this as our headline result. It was not.' Claim the framing as UNCOMMON, not unprecedented.
